enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **g)** Write a letter to your guardian thanking him/her for having sponsored you in school. Also say the plans you have for the family. Your name is Afukang and your address is P.O Box 333 Nkatta
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Sender's address (P.O Box 333, Nkatta) and date at top right; salutation to the guardian.
2. Opening: greetings and the purpose of the letter, thanks for sponsoring the schooling.
3. Specific things the sponsorship made possible (fees, books, results).
4. Plans for the family (help the younger ones, build a good house, start a small business).
5. Promise to work hard; closing wishes and subscription; name Afukang.

**Model composition (460 words)**

P.O Box 333
Nkatta
10th July 2026

Dear Uncle,

I hope this letter finds you and Auntie in good health and in high spirits. As for me, I am well, and I thank God for His mercies.

I am writing to thank you from the bottom of my heart for sponsoring my education. When my father passed away, I thought my school days were over, and I could see no way out. You stepped in without being asked, and you have paid my fees, bought my uniforms and books and even given me pocket money every term. Because of your support, I have never been sent out of class for unpaid fees, and I recently passed my General Certificate of Education Ordinary Level examination in six subjects. Everybody in the village says that I am lucky to have a guardian like you, and I agree.

Your kindness has not only changed my life but also given me a dream. I have decided to continue to the Advanced Level and, later, to study medicine at the university. My plan is to come back and work in our own community, where many families have to walk more than ten kilometres to reach a health centre.

I know that you have also sacrificed your own comfort for me. Your children needed new clothes and shoes, yet you never made me feel like a burden, and you treated me as your own child. I shall never forget this generosity, and I pray that I will repay it one day. Last term, I came third in my class, and my teachers have promised to support my application for a scholarship at the Advanced Level.

I also have plans for the family. Once I begin to earn a salary, my first duty will be to pay the school fees of my younger brothers and sisters, so that they do not suffer as I almost did. I shall help my mother to replace the leaking roof of our house with iron sheets and to start a small shop in front of the compound. With the rest of my income, I want to set up a scholarship for one poor child every year, so that your good deed will be repeated in the lives of others.

In the meantime, I promise you that I shall work very hard and shall never waste the opportunity that you have given me. I will respect my teachers, avoid bad company and spend my holidays reading and helping at home. I shall make you proud.

Please give my warm greetings to Auntie and to my cousins. May God bless you abundantly and give you long life and good health, so that you will see the fruits of your labour.

Yours lovingly,

Afukang

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | The letter thanks the guardian AND states plans for the family, in the correct informal layout (address, date, salutation, closing, name) |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, a style and tone suited to the topic, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Using a wrong address or a different name from the one imposed by the topic (Afukang, P.O Box 333 Nkatta).
2. Forgetting the plans for the family, or using a formal layout and an over-formal tone.
